title: Finite etale covers of the closed fibre of a proper scheme over a henselian pair lift
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, let $Y\to S$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $Y_0=Y\times_SS_0$, with closed immersion $i:Y_0\to Y$. Then for every finite etale $Y_0$-scheme $V\to Y_0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] there exist a finite etale $Y$-scheme $U\to Y$ and an isomorphism of $Y_0$-schemes $U\times_YY_0\cong V$; i.e. the base change functor $i^*:\mathsf{FEt}(Y)\to\mathsf{FEt}(Y_0)$ is essentially surjective.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair), the three essential-surjectivity parts of its proof: (i) A Noetherian and I-adically complete (Etale Morphisms Theorem 039R remarkable equivalence, More on Morphisms thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian, Grothendieck algebraization Cohomology of Schemes algebraize-formal-scheme-finite-over-proper, More on Morphisms check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds, specialization to the closed fibre); (ii) (A, I) henselian with A a Noetherian G-ring (completion, Limits descend-finite-presentation/descend-finite-finite-presentation/descend-etale, Smoothing Ring Maps lemma-henselian-pair approximation); (iii) general case (Limits proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation-noetherian, More on Algebra henselization-colimit, henselization-pair-G-ring, ubiquity-G-ring). The henselian local case is Lemma 0A48 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian), same proof.

proof.text: First assume that A is Noetherian and I-adically complete. Formal etaleness and invariance of the etale site under nilpotent thickenings lift V uniquely to a compatible system of finite etale covers V_r of Y_r=Y\times_A Spec(A/I^{r+1}). Finiteness is preserved because it can be checked on a finite affine cover and lifted generators remain finite by Nakayama. Grothendieck existence for finite morphisms over a proper scheme algebraizes the compatible system to a finite morphism U\to Y with closed fibre V. Its etale locus is open and contains V; since U is proper over the local base, every nonempty closed complement meets the closed fibre, so the locus is all of U. Thus U is finite etale.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma 0GS2, complete Noetherian case

proof.text: If A is a Noetherian henselian G-ring, complete it. The preceding construction gives a finite etale cover after completion. A finite affine cover of Y, finite generators and relations for the cover algebras, overlap maps, and cocycle equations form finite presentation data. Descend this data to a finite type A-algebra inside the completion; after enlarging the stage the descended morphism is finite etale. Henselian G-ring approximation supplies a solution in A congruent modulo I to the completed solution, and hence a finite etale Y-scheme whose closed fibre is V.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma 0GS2, Noetherian G-ring case

proof.text: For a general henselian pair, write A as a filtered colimit of henselian localizations of finite type Noetherian G-ring models. Properness and finite presentation descend to a model Y_j. The finite etale cover V, its affine generators and relations, and all overlap and cocycle equations descend to one common index; finite-presentation descent also identifies the closed-fibre cover after base change. Applying the Noetherian G-ring case at that index and base-changing back to A produces a finite etale lift of V.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma 0GS2, general henselian-pair case

proof.text: The construction is functorial under base change to Y_0, so the resulting finite etale U comes with the required Y_0-isomorphism U\times_YY_0\cong V. This is precisely essential surjectivity of the restriction functor.

split_report.summary: Split the Stacks 0GS2 essential-surjectivity proof into complete Noetherian algebraization, Noetherian G-ring approximation, and general henselian finite-presentation limit descent. The final step identifies the resulting closed fibre with the given finite etale cover. Each new node has LeanSearch, Loogle/LeanFinder, and Mathlib source grep records; no matching Mathlib theorem exists.
